headline: IRGC Navy claims 7 oil tankers hit/damaged in one night (4 set on fire, 3 struck mines)
dek: IRGC Navy claims its forces hit and set fire to 4 tankers transferring oil 'through an illegal route' despite warnings, and 3 more vessels struck mines in western Hormuz overnight; warns it will target US bases if the US keeps facilitating passage through 'illegally mined' routes.
sources: IRGC Navy statement via Iranian state television (IRIB), carried by Reuters
fault_line: Is Iran legitimately enforcing wartime control over its own strait against US-escorted 'illegal route' traffic — or manufacturing a 7-ship night to squeeze leverage ahead of Israel's Oct 27 election and US midterms?

sections.what_happened: IRGC Navy claims its forces hit and set fire to 4 tankers transferring oil 'through an illegal route' despite warnings, and 3 more vessels struck mines in western Hormuz overnight; warns it will target US bases if the US keeps facilitating passage through 'illegally mined' routes.
sections.what_verified: Reuters carried the IRIB report; PTI/AP summary notes AP could not independently verify; multiple regional outlets (New Indian Express, Business Standard, Daily Sabah, Lokmat Times, Mathrubhumi, Free Press Journal) ran the same IRGC-sourced account.
sections.what_disputed: UKMTO (British maritime monitor) did NOT report the incidents; Iran's claim names no vessels, flags, or casualties. Monitors note shippers' growing reluctance to report incidents, so absence of UKMTO entries is not proof of absence. Guardian editorial (Oct 22) quoted IRGC saying a return to war is 'unlikely' — tonal tension with the warning, not a factual contradiction.
sections.why_matters: Iran's side, primary-source treatment: the Iranian Navy is enforcing sovereignty over a waterway it has controlled through 8 months of war; US escort of ships through mined 'illegal passages' is the provocation; the base-strike warning is deterrence while Araghchi's seven-day initiative keeps the door to Islamabad talks open. Label everything as Iran's claim; note UKMTO silence honestly.
sections.context: Background: Hormuz — NEW (overnight Oct 21-22): IRGC Navy claims 7 oil tankers hit/damaged in one night (4 set on fire, 3 struck mines); warns US bases if Washington keeps escorting ships

totw_analysis: Our read: Iran's side, primary-source treatment: the Iranian Navy is enforcing sovereignty over a waterway it has controlled through 8 months of war; US escort of ships through mined 'illegal passages' is the provocation; the base-strike warning is deterrence while Araghchi's seven-day initiative keeps the door to Islamabad talks open. Label everything as Iran's claim; note UKMTO silence honestly. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Iran legitimately enforcing wartime control over its own strait against US-escorted 'illegal route' traffic — or manufacturing a 7-ship night to squeeze leverage ahead of Israel's Oct 27 election and US midterms?
